evidence.quote: An 83-year-old male, living alone and independently, presented to St. Ann’s Hospital Wound Clinic on December 29, 2017.
Initial presentation as related by the patient and family included a hematoma on the medial portion of the right calf, tingling in the right leg and foot, and some weakness of the involved extremity.
Over the next 24-48 hours, the patient and family reported that the hematoma increased in size and severity resulting in significant wound involvement and tissue necrosis
This increase in the severity of symptoms prompted their visit to St. Ann’s Hospital Wound Clinic, Westerville, Ohio.

summary.text: An 83-year-old male presented to a hospital wound clinic on December 29, 2017 after a calf injury, attributed by the author to sustained external compression; the patient and family gave differing accounts of how it happened. A hematoma on the medial right calf, tingling and some weakness at first received watchful waiting, then enlarged over 24-48 hours with wound involvement and tissue necrosis. Examination showed extensive soft tissue damage with muscle necrosis and intact pulses.

He was admitted for workup; imaging showed no fractures. Surgery included hematoma evacuation, extensive debridement of necrotic tissue including muscle, pulsed lavage and deep tissue cultures. The author favored compartment syndrome sequela over hematoma alone, and surgical wound cultures were negative other than skin flora.

NPWTi-d with a VeraFlo foam dressing was started in the operating room after surgery and given during a six-day hospital stay, with hypergranular changes at 48 hours. He moved to a skilled nursing facility on traditional NPWT. About six weeks from surgery the wound bed was granular, NPWT stopped, and automated suction blister epidermal grafting was chosen and repeated three times.

Paresthesias and limb pain resolved within the first postoperative month. Complete closure was reported about six weeks after the third grafting and at six months, with ambulation and normal limb function in about two months. He recovered without loss of sensation or function, kept his limb, and returned to an assisted living environment.

ambiguities.issue: Two accounts of the injury mechanism: the patient said he fell into a bar stool at home, while upon further exploration the family felt he fell asleep in his power recliner with the right leg lodged in the footrest hinge. The author states the etiology as sustained external compression trauma to the calf. "Less than a week prior" grammatically dates the patient statement, not the injury itself.

evidence.quote: Less than a week prior, he stated to the family that "I fell into a bar stool at home."
the family felt that he fell asleep in his power recliner resulting in his right leg being lodged in the hinge portion of the footrest

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide which account is correct; both accounts are review-only and only the author-stated etiology is scored.

ambiguities.issue: Residence: the patient is described as living alone and independently at presentation, and later as returning to an assisted living environment where he resided at initial presentation. The two descriptions concern different attributes (living arrangement vs residence type) and are not mutually exclusive, so this is an ambiguity, not a source conflict.

evidence.quote: living alone and independently
Ultimately he returned to an assisted living environment where he resided at initial presentation.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer that independent living was within an assisted living facility, or that either statement is wrong.

ambiguities.issue: Complete closure is stated about six weeks after the third grafting (case presentation) and at six months (discussion and Figure 13-14 captions); the reference point of "six months" is not stated. Different anchors, not two values for one time.

Complete wound closure was seen in six months.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not compute or reconcile an interval between the two statements, and do not treat them as one measurement.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the 14 JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual target.

Injury mechanism differs between the patient (fall into a bar stool) and the family (leg lodged in a recliner footrest); both accounts are review-only and the author-stated compression etiology is kept.
Residence is described both as living alone and independently and as an assisted living environment at initial presentation; recorded as an ambiguity, not a conflict.
Complete closure is stated both about six weeks after the third grafting and at six months; the anchor of six months is not stated, so both are kept without reconciliation.
Compartment syndrome sequela is a hedged author diagnosis (favored over hematoma alone) and is recorded as provisional.
No laboratory values, antibiotic names or measurements are reported; deep tissue cultures and the later surgical wound culture result are not linked.
Introduction, literature-review sentences and the author general practice with other irrigants are background and not patient facts.
